payload.claim: The floor-vs-used decision for the max-peak row is `any("error_max_turns" in e for e in turns_row.endings)`, which is meant to catch a ceiling-hit anywhere among that row's abnormal endings — but every witness for this line (`test_the_ceilings_line_calls_a_cut_off_rows_peak_a_floor`) only ever gives a row a single-element `endings` list. A regression that only inspects the first ending (e.g. `"error_max_turns" in turns_row.endings[0]` guarded by non-empty) would pass both existing assertions unchanged, yet mislabel a real row like the one already exercised at line 803-806 (`endings == ["IMPLEMENTING error_max_turns", "REBUTTING error_max_budget_usd (...)"]`-shaped, but with the ceiling hit second) as `used` instead of `a floor`, reintroducing exactly the false-blocker misreading this spec exists to fix. Adding a case with two endings where `error_max_turns` is not the first element would force the general (not first-only) implementation to stay distinguishable.
